items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive agent app, against ChatGPT Dots and Meta Muse
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude Duet page describes a proactive agent that takes tasks by message, works in the cloud using connected apps and messages the user when done or when it needs a decision. It offers a morning brief, asks approval before sensitive actions such as sending messages or paying, and reuses the user's Claude memory, skills and apps. It is a research preview on a waitlist for US Claude Pro and Max subscribers, as a standalone iOS/Android app and on claude.ai.
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic is moving from chat and coding toward an always-on consumer agent, entering the category OpenAI and Meta have just launched; usage counts against existing plan limits rather than a new price.

items.title: Anthropic: Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins; 17 of 211 designs bound in the lab
items.summary: Anthropic asked an internal research Claude model to design minibinders against five scorpion neurotoxins. Over about 64 hours, 10,000 GPU hours and 12 design tools, Claude generated 318,484 designs and 211 were tested by Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience. 17 (about 8%) met the binder criteria, and the best binders to toxin Cn2 reached single-digit nanomolar KD. All designs and data are on Hugging Face.
items.why_it_matters: It is a concrete, lab-validated example of an LLM running a design campaign end to end, though the hit rate is typical for the field and no neutralisation or animal data exist yet.

sources.title: How Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins

items.confidence_note: Anthropic says only recombinant toxins were tested; no cell neutralisation or animal efficacy data, and it does not claim an antivenom. Published Oct 20, inside the 6h-earlier allowance only because the harvest first saw it at 17:03Z.

items.title: Huang at GTC Berlin: pre-integrated DSX POD cuts AI-factory site deployment from about six months to as little as 14 days
items.original_title: 黄仁勋柏林演讲：AI工厂部署最快缩至14天，智能体安全是技术问题
items.summary: The Paper reports that at GTC Berlin on 21 Oct, Jensen Huang presented the DSX POD, a pre-integrated and pre-tested design of seven liquid-cooled racks on 800V DC power, which he said can shorten on-site deployment from roughly six months to as little as 14 days once site infrastructure is ready, with partner deliveries planned from early 2027. He said Vera Rubin is in full production with single-node assembly under 5 minutes versus 2 hours for Grace Blackwell, and framed agent security as an engineering problem, backed by an OpenShell reference architecture. The article puts a 1 GW AI factory at about $50B build cost and about $40B yearly revenue, figures it derives from the talk.
items.why_it_matters: Faster, pre-fabricated deployment targets the grid-and-construction bottleneck that has slowed AI capacity, a selling point for Europe's sovereign-AI push and a competitive pressure on Chinese server and datacentre builders.
key_numbers: Deployment: ~6 months to as little as 14 days
Vera Rubin node assembly <5 min vs 2 h

items.title: Anthropic: Claude found 493 attack-surface issues across 25 open-source projects, including unneeded OpenSSH pre-auth code
items.summary: Anthropic describes using Claude to reduce the attack surface of code rather than hunt individual bugs. Across 25 open-source projects (5M+ lines) it found 493 issues and catalogued 17,000+ configuration options, 3,842 security-relevant. In OpenSSH, about 4,500 lines of experimental ML-DSA-44 code (roughly 16% of default pre-auth code) were reachable by unauthenticated clients; the fix in 10.6 removed about a fifth of such reachable code. Anthropic packaged the method as a three-pass Claude skill.
items.why_it_matters: It shifts AI security work from finding exploitable bugs to removing code and risky config combinations before they are exploitable, a cheaper defensive lever for maintainers.

sources.title: Using Claude to reduce the attack surface of code

items.confidence_note: Figures are from the Anthropic page via a summarising fetch; publication time is an estimate from the HN listing.

items.title: OpenAI adds 12-hour cache retention option; Chinese tech press contrasts it with DeepSeek's longer cache design
items.original_title: 永久保留缓存！OpenAI重磅更新，比DeepSeek还久？
items.summary: Ifeng Tech (republishing Zhidx) reports OpenAI's API now offers prompt-cache retention of 30 minutes by default or 12 hours as an option, for GPT-5.6 and later, with cache-write pricing rising from 1.25x to 2.5x the uncached input price while reads are unchanged. Codex and Work log-in users are said to get 'permanent' cache, which the article suspects means free recomputation rather than true storage. It contrasts this with DeepSeek's newly open-sourced framework, which it says targets three days of cache retention.
items.why_it_matters: Cache lifetime and write pricing now decide agent-workflow costs, and Chinese outlets are using DeepSeek's cheap long-lived cache as the benchmark OpenAI is judged against.
key_numbers: Cache-write price 1.25x to 2.5x input with 12 h option
